thread:
zoe: Quick note 1 I'm prototyping request-folding (combine concurrent requests into one auth call) at the edge to cut auth RPS. Need input on quota/billing and audit implications.

nate: Sounds good. Key constraint: billing wants per-request granularity. If we fold, we must preserve per-request attribution somewhere.

quinn: Two practical options: 1) edge expands and writes N events to billing (bad for IO), 2) edge writes one compact envelope + telemetry pipeline expands to N events later. I prefer 2.

zoe: Agreed on envelope. We'd include per-item metadata (org, project, sa, request_id, token_hash) but only token_hash, not raw token. auth-bot: (automated) Reminder: do not log raw tokens; token_hash allowed.

nate: For quotas, auth service should run per-item attribution and emit quota-usage per item so counting stays correct. Also need idempotency keys to avoid double-burn on retries.

quinn: Add trace_id to envelope so console can link expanded events back to the original folded call. Console UX: show folded totals and offer "expand" to see per-request rows.

zoe: Rollout plan: canary 2% traffic, mirror expanded events during canary, compare billing parity for a few hours before ramp. Add metric: "quota_mismatch_rate" and auto-fallback if >0.1%.

nate: I'll draft envelope schema and idempotency scheme (token_hash+req_id+minute).

quinn: I'll stub runbook for oncall to detect and revert.

zoe: Thanks 1 putting a draft PR up, will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
